newsitem.title: SPAIN: Bomb explodes in Barcelona, no casualties.
newsitem.headline: Bomb explodes in Barcelona, no casualties.

text.p: A bomb exploded at a Barcelona radio station on Friday, causing damage but no injuries, station officials said.

A spokeswoman for COM Radio said there was no reason to believe the blast was linked to the Basque guerrilla group ETA. The separatist rebels killed a Basque politician last week, sparking protests throughout Spain.
Despite that, the station's director said an anonymous caller speaking in the Basque language phoned on Thursday and declared "Long live the Basque country."
Two men in business suits delivered a package on Friday morning. A cleaning woman moved it, and minutes later it exploded, the station's spokeswoman said.
Police declined to provide details about the blast, but said it was a home-made bomb and was similar to other improvised devices that exploded in Barcelona's cathedral and had no links to ETA.
Spanish authorities have been on a high state of alert this week fearing further attacks by Basque guerrillas following the killing of 29-year-old Miguel Angel Blanco.
ETA sympathisers and offices of the group's political arm, Herri Batasuna, have been targeted for sporadic attacks in recent days. Police are concerned that ETA may retaliate with more violence.
